title: Three Seasons and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：score　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 score 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the coach ① kept the score that no player in the field would have recorded, and he said the keeping was the whole of the season. The ② score, meaning the mark itself and not the whistle, ran three seasons and stayed unrecorded in the book; a score, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ score in that field had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ score at the far stand, meaning the goal they kept for the children to cheer and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A score, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the coach said the recording is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the score was the whole of the matter, meaning the judgement and not the mark. The ⑥ score, meaning the judgement and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; score, he said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both a mark and a judgement. He said the judgement is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ score had become a line in a record, and the record had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ score of the whole thing, the coach wrote in April, was one field and three seasons of recording; score, he said, is either the goal at the far stand or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ score I remember is the mark recorded in the record, which closed in 1993 and is still recorded as the quietest in the field. A ⑩ score, my mother said in 1995, is the only mark that improves by being recorded; every score, she said, is a judgement that has agreed to look like a mark. She said the judgement was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 分数；比分（指球场里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 分数；比分（指那分分数本身，与小小的哨子相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep the score 记这一分分数
D. n. 分数；比分（指留给孩子们喊的那一个）
E. n. 分数之事（抽象总称，指一处球场的分数之事）
F. n. 分数；比分（指赛事记录里写到、被记载的那一分）
G. n. 分数、评断（指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 评断（抽象总称，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: kept the score that no player in the field would have recorded

the score at the far stand

answers.why: keep the score 意为“记这一分分数”，1986 年那位教练把球场里没有一位队员肯记载的一分分数做了一遍。
score 意为“分数；比分”，指那分分数本身而不是小小的哨子，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被记载。
score 意为“分数；比分”，指球场里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一只小小的哨子。
score 意为“分数；比分”，指最远那面看台的留给孩子们喊的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
score 意为“分数、评断”，指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这分评断就是那件事的全部。
score 意为“评断”，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西而不是那分分数，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
score 意为“分数；比分”，指赛事记录里写到、被记载的那一分，到 1991 年这一分成了赛事记录里的一行。
score 意为“分数之事”，教练四月写道，整件事的分数之事是一处球场和三个赛季的记载。
score 意为“分数；比分”，我记得的是赛事记录里记载过的那一分，1993 年打完了，至今仍被说成球场里最安静的一分。
score 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，分数是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的分数。
